unit: words of the whole file, as `LC_ALL=C wc -w` counts them: a SKILL.md keyed by its skill's directory, frontmatter included, and a role file beside it keyed `<skill>/<file>`
raise: only in the commit that needs it, recorded in `raises` as {"from": <old>, "to": <new>, "why": "<the sentence skill-retro Step 4 asks for>"}; `skill-lint.py --against <ref>` fails a rise without one

skill-retro.why: Step 2 names the linter's new check, a `$` followed by a digit in a SKILL.md, which the Skill tool replaces with an argument when the skill loads: on 2026-10-21 harden's awk `$0` loaded as the first argument word, and a `{print $1}` in resolve-ticket's PRS lookup loaded as `{print --plan-only}`, so the five awk programs now use $NF, $(NF-1) and $(NF-NF)

pr-harden.why: State says that where CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG is on a live agent can outlast the gates' one-hour await bound, since its requests wait at a usage limit for the reset and the harness does not report it stalled (measured against a stub, artifacts/2026-10-21-retry-watchdog-limit), and that nothing in the session marks that hour, so the gate's block opens on such an await and the run records it again with the command that recorded it, --only and --run included, rather than re-dispatching its phase beside the live agent; once, a name listed twice being that once spent, after which the agent is stopped with TaskStop before the dead-phase contract retries its phase; the rule moves here from resolve-ticket's Step 1 because resolve-ticket's alias reaches a standalone pr-harden or harden too

pr-harden/fixer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the fixer the key, nothing it commits names it or the ticket's URL, in the message, a comment, a test name or a changeSet id, the message describes what the code now does in its own words, and it runs the pre-push check before reporting its sha, so the sha the verifier runs is the one pushed; it rewrites rather than only amends, building again if that changed a file; and the brief gives it the PR's number to fetch with, keeping any message file outside the worktree, and reporting a squash a merge stops instead of looping on it

pr-harden/reviewer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the ticket's key, and that the PR's silence about the ticket, and a body without the loop's declines, is deliberate and not a finding

resolve-ticket/refuter.md.why: the plan refuter's seven questions, the JSON it returns and the rule every objection must meet move here from SKILL.md byte for byte, beneath a new header that tells it to read the file first and what its brief carries, the shape pr-harden 0.36.0 gave the fixer and the verifier, once role-file-check's wave 1 passed (2026-09-28). The header and SKILL.md's pointer are new text, so resolve-ticket grows by both, for a refuter that reads its questions as written

resolve-ticket.why: Step 1 pre-flights the usage limit beside the verifier: a claude.ai usage limit ends the turn on an API error, which runs StopFailure rather than Stop, so no gate sees it, while under CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG a request at the limit waits for the reset inside the turn (both measured against a stub, artifacts/2026-10-21-retry-watchdog-limit); so an interactive run prints the variable and the running binary's version through CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH and, unless the variable is 1, true, yes or on in any case and the version reads 2.1.301 (Claude Code) or later, compared number by number, says so at once and carries on, giving the remedy for later sessions as Claude Code 2.1.301 or later started through a literal shell alias with a five-hour usage-limit wait cap, or the same two variables before pool-run --work, never settings.json env, which reaches the driver's headless sessions that pool-run otherwise keeps the pair out of, and never a mid-run relaunch; and a wait can hold a live agent past the gates' one-hour await bound, which the paragraph's last sentence points to pr-harden's State for

pr-review.why: Step 1 gains two sentences: a 404 from the JIRA endpoint can be a private ticket, so it is read with getJiraIssue, asking for the comment field it leaves out by default; and a ticket only that reads, or a PR the local PRS file lists, is private, so nothing posted on the PR names, quotes or links its ticket or says what the code let an attacker do; and where nothing settles a 404, as in CI, it says only that the tracker was unreachable

pr-review/posting.md.why: the first gate line says that on a private PR nothing posted names, quotes or links its ticket, whatever the third line's link rule asks, or says what the code let an attacker do, so a local run recites it before it posts or stages; the rule itself lives in SKILL.md, which the @claude review Action loads alone

ticket-pool.why: the sentence listing what a ticket argument may be says a private ticket's JIRA key is never one and not to queue one, because the pool cannot tell it from a missing key, its headless sessions cannot read it, and its driver writes a record named for the key into the store skill-retro publishes

ticket-pool/pausing.md.why: the paragraph on which sessions the --work carry reaches says what carries a session started by hand besides Claude Code's own wait, CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG, which resolve-ticket's Step 1 says how to set, so the two skills no longer disagree about whether such a session can be carried past a usage limit; and the driver's own carry says Session drops that variable and its cap from every headless session it starts, limit probes included, since one waiting under them never shows the driver its limit, while a settings.json env still reaches them (measured against a stub)

harden.why: the paragraph that bounds the gate's await allow at an hour says a usage-limit wait can have held the agent past it, that the gate's block then opens on that await, and that pr-harden's State says what it gets, since under CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG an agent waiting at a limit is alive and unreported past that hour, and past it the gate's block otherwise said Run Phase 2 once
